{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Adopt Java 17+ as the baseline JDK, as required by Spring Framework 6.0.",
    "Leverage and extend existing Spring Cloud Data YARN modules and contracts as the foundation.",
    "Integrate Spring Boot's JarLauncher API for module launching and classpath management (refactoring from ModuleLauncher) to eliminate duplicate code and simplify dependency handling.",

    "Support configurable deployment properties (module-specific yarn.app.name, queues, memory/CPU) via Spring's property resolution mechanisms.",
    "Implement external library resolution by scanning module manifests for dependencies, downloading them to a local cache, and appending them to the Spring Boot application classpath before launch.",
    "Develop comprehensive unit and integration tests using mocking frameworks (e.g., Mockito) for external dependencies (HDFS, YARN REST APIs).",
    "Documentation will include developer guides, configuration references, and test case descriptions."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The developer has existing familiarity with the Spring Cloud Data YARN codebase, Spring Boot, YARN, HDFS, and REST API integration.",
    "The existing codebase has a clear architecture (e.g., deployer interfaces, configuration models) that can be extended for new functionality.",
    "A suitable development environment is available with access to a Hadoop/YARN cluster or emulators for integration testing.",
    "All external libraries required by OOTB modules are publicly available or accessible from a standard Maven repository.",
    "The scope is limited to the development effort (coding, unit/integration testing within a dev environment), excluding full system testing in a production-like environment, performance tuning, or release packaging.",
    "Assume existing unit and integration test suites exist and can be extended; the estimate includes adding new tests but not rewriting all legacy tests.",
    "Documentation is written in Markdown and included in the project repository."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Implement HDFS Auto-Deployment for YARN Apps (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement the component responsible for automatically packaging or placing a YARN application's artifacts into HDFS upon deployment request, as orchestrated by xd-admin via manifest configuration. Includes configuration parsing, HDFS client interaction, error handling, and unit tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Implement REST API Negotiation for Group Deployment (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Develop a module that communicates with the YARN ResourceManager's REST APIs to deploy application modules in groups. This includes handling app-specific metadata (e.g., appType, appName), parsing deployment groups, and providing instrumentation hooks. Includes REST client development, configuration, integration, and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Support Multiple YARN App Instances via Configuration (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Extend the deployment property model and configuration parsing to allow different application instances (with potentially different names, queues, priorities, and resource reservations) to be defined per module or stream using properties like `module.*.yarn.app.name`. Includes design of property schema, implementation, and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Make Deployer Work Asynchronously (U4)",
      "activity_description": "Refactor the core deployment flow to operate asynchronously, allowing the shell command to return immediately while deployment tasks are queued and executed within YARN. Involves designing an asynchronous architecture (e.g., using Spring's @Async or a task queue), integrating with the existing deployer, and ensuring proper status reporting. Includes design, implementation, and testing.",
      "most_likely_effort": 22.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Refactor Module Launcher to Use Spring Boot's JarLauncher (U5, U6)",
      "activity_description": "Refactor the existing ModuleLauncher contract to integrate with Spring Boot's JarLauncher API. This consolidates module launching logic, provides a standard mechanism for resolving and loading module-dependent JARs onto the Boot classpath, and removes duplicate functionality. Includes analysis of both APIs, code refactoring, implementation of the new launcher, and comprehensive unit/integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Document and Write Test Cases for JAR Resolution (U7)",
      "activity_description": "Complete the documentation (developer guide, configuration reference) and write detailed test cases specifically for the new mechanism of resolving and adding module-dependent JARs to the Boot loader (as implemented in A5). This documentation serves as a reference for porting modules with external dependencies. Includes writing docs, designing test scenarios, and implementing test cases.",
      "most_likely_effort": 18.0
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Add Support for External Library Dependencies (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement a unified way to handle and consume external library dependencies specified by modules. This builds upon the JarLauncher refactoring (A5) by adding logic to resolve declared external JARs (e.g., from a local or remote repository), manage a cache, and ensure they are available to the module's classloader at runtime. Includes design, implementation, and tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16.0
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 140.0
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt Java 17+ as the baseline JDK, as required by Spring Framework 6.0.
Leverage and extend existing Spring Cloud Data YARN modules and contracts as the foundation.
Integrate Spring Boot's JarLauncher API for module launching and classpath management (refactoring from ModuleLauncher) to eliminate duplicate code and simplify dependency handling.
Implement asynchronous deployment using a task queue pattern (e.g., Spring Integration or a custom executor) integrated with YARN's ResourceManager to return control to the shell quickly.
Use Hadoop Client APIs (e.g., FileSystem) for HDFS operations and Spring's RestTemplate/WebClient for ResourceManager REST API communication.
Support configurable deployment properties (module-specific yarn.app.name, queues, memory/CPU) via Spring's property resolution mechanisms.
Implement external library resolution by scanning module manifests for dependencies, downloading them to a local cache, and appending them to the Spring Boot application classpath before launch.
Develop comprehensive unit and integration tests using mocking frameworks (e.g., Mockito) for external dependencies (HDFS, YARN REST APIs).
Documentation will include developer guides, configuration references, and test case descriptions.
assumptions: The developer has existing familiarity with the Spring Cloud Data YARN codebase, Spring Boot, YARN, HDFS, and REST API integration.
The existing codebase has a clear architecture (e.g., deployer interfaces, configuration models) that can be extended for new functionality.
A suitable development environment is available with access to a Hadoop/YARN cluster or emulators for integration testing.
All external libraries required by OOTB modules are publicly available or accessible from a standard Maven repository.

The scope is limited to the development effort (coding, unit/integration testing within a dev environment), excluding full system testing in a production-like environment, performance tuning, or release packaging.
Assume existing unit and integration test suites exist and can be extended; the estimate includes adding new tests but not rewriting all legacy tests.
Documentation is written in Markdown and included in the project repository.

activities.activity_name: Implement HDFS Auto-Deployment for YARN Apps (U1)
activities.activity_description: Design and implement the component responsible for automatically packaging or placing a YARN application's artifacts into HDFS upon deployment request, as orchestrated by xd-admin via manifest configuration. Includes configuration parsing, HDFS client interaction, error handling, and unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Implement REST API Negotiation for Group Deployment (U2)
activities.activity_description: Develop a module that communicates with the YARN ResourceManager's REST APIs to deploy application modules in groups. This includes handling app-specific metadata (e.g., appType, appName), parsing deployment groups, and providing instrumentation hooks. Includes REST client development, configuration, integration, and tests.

activities.activity_name: Support Multiple YARN App Instances via Configuration (U3)
activities.activity_description: Extend the deployment property model and configuration parsing to allow different application instances (with potentially different names, queues, priorities, and resource reservations) to be defined per module or stream using properties like `module.*.yarn.app.name`. Includes design of property schema, implementation, and tests.

Refactor the core deployment flow to operate asynchronously, allowing the shell command to return immediately while deployment tasks are queued and executed within YARN. Involves designing an asynchronous architecture (e.g., using Spring's @Async or a task queue), integrating with the existing deployer, and ensuring proper status reporting. Includes design, implementation, and testing.

activities.activity_name: Refactor Module Launcher to Use Spring Boot's JarLauncher (U5, U6)
activities.activity_description: Refactor the existing ModuleLauncher contract to integrate with Spring Boot's JarLauncher API. This consolidates module launching logic, provides a standard mechanism for resolving and loading module-dependent JARs onto the Boot classpath, and removes duplicate functionality. Includes analysis of both APIs, code refactoring, implementation of the new launcher, and comprehensive unit/integration tests.

activities.activity_name: Document and Write Test Cases for JAR Resolution (U7)
activities.activity_description: Complete the documentation (developer guide, configuration reference) and write detailed test cases specifically for the new mechanism of resolving and adding module-dependent JARs to the Boot loader (as implemented in A5). This documentation serves as a reference for porting modules with external dependencies. Includes writing docs, designing test scenarios, and implementing test cases.

activities.activity_name: Add Support for External Library Dependencies (U8)
activities.activity_description: Design and implement a unified way to handle and consume external library dependencies specified by modules. This builds upon the JarLauncher refactoring (A5) by adding logic to resolve declared external JARs (e.g., from a local or remote repository), manage a cache, and ensure they are available to the module's classloader at runtime. Includes design, implementation, and tests.
